issue: Role-collection for 'BMS Admin' references '$XSAPPNAME.admin' (a scope reference) not a role-template reference. The correct format for role-template-references is '$XSAPPNAME.BMS_ADMIN'. Using the scope directly means the role-collection does not include any additional scopes bundled in the BMS_ADMIN role-template (manage, operate, inspect, view, certify, config_manager, executive_view, external_view). BMS Admins deployed via this mta.yaml will only have the 'admin' scope.
fix: Change '$XSAPPNAME.admin' to '$XSAPPNAME.BMS_ADMIN' in the BMS Admin role-collection entry at mta.yaml line 262.

issue: health-check-type is set to 'none' for BridgeManagement-srv. Cloud Foundry will not restart the app if it enters a deadlocked state or stops responding to HTTP requests. SAP BTP Certified App criteria require a proper HTTP health check endpoint.
fix: Set health-check-type to 'http' and health-check-http-endpoint to '/health' (or '/'). Ensure the CAP server responds 200 on that path (srv/server.js already has a /health endpoint).

issue: MTA version is 1.7.2 but APP_VERSION property on the srv module is hardcoded to '1.0.0-nsw-standalone'. These two versions are out of sync. The app-version badge shown in the shell will display '1.0.0-nsw-standalone' while the MTA/deployment version is 1.7.2. This causes confusion during incident triage and is a PAC audit red flag.
fix: Set APP_VERSION to '${version}' (MTA built-in placeholder) to automatically pick up the mta.yaml version, or keep them manually aligned.

issue: No BTP Connectivity Service declared in mta.yaml resources or required by BridgeManagement-srv. srv/external-api.js makes outbound HTTP calls to external APIs (BNAC, NHVR). In SAP BTP Cloud Foundry, outbound HTTP to external hosts requires the Connectivity Service + Cloud Connector for on-premise targets or named Destinations for internet-facing endpoints. The current setup works locally but will silently fail or produce connection-refused errors in BTP production.
fix: Either (a) add 'BridgeManagement-connectivity' resource (type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service, service: connectivity, service-plan: lite) and add it to the srv module's requires list; or (b) route all outbound calls through the Destination Service using named HTTP destinations configured in BTP cockpit.

issue: BridgeManagement-destination service uses service-plan 'lite'. The 'lite' plan has a hard limit on destinations and does not support proxy-type OnPremise. If future on-premise connectivity is required (e.g. S/4HANA integration via Cloud Connector), this plan must be upgraded to 'standard'. Also the 'lite' plan for application-logs (line 306) has a retention limit that may not meet audit log retention requirements under Privacy Act APP11.
fix: Evaluate upgrading destination service-plan to 'standard' before go-live if on-premise/S4 connectivity is planned. Evaluate upgrading application-logs plan to 'standard' for extended retention.

issue: The appSubTitle in admin-bridges i18n.properties reads 'CAP Sample Application' — a scaffolding placeholder that appears in the FLP shell header and browser tab title for the Bridge Asset Registry app, which is a government production system. This will be flagged in any SAP PAC review or government accessibility audit as unprofessional/incomplete.
fix: Change appSubTitle from 'CAP Sample Application' to a production-appropriate subtitle such as 'Bridge Asset Registry — Transport for NSW'.

issue: console.log is used in a production code path — the request logging middleware calls console.log for every successful HTTP response. In SAP BTP Cloud Foundry, console.log bypasses the structured logging format expected by the BridgeManagement-logging (application-logs) service. This produces unstructured log noise and makes correlation-id based log queries unreliable. ISO 25010 Maintainability score: 2/5.
fix: Replace the console.log call in the request logger with cds.log('request').info(entry) so logs flow through the CAP logging infrastructure and are indexed by correlationId in Application Logs.

issue: All 12 navigation item labels in the BMS Admin shell side-nav are hardcoded English strings (e.g. 'Change Documents', 'Data Quality', 'GIS Config') with no i18n key binding. The i18n.properties file has corresponding keys (admin.changeDocuments.title, admin.gisConfig.title) but they are not used in the view. This prevents localisation and violates SAP Fiori i18n guidelines.
fix: Replace each hardcoded text attribute with an i18n binding: e.g. text="{i18n>admin.changeDocuments.title}". Add missing keys to i18n.properties for nav items that do not yet have entries.

issue: The shell header Title text 'BMS Administration' is hardcoded and not externalised to i18n. In a multi-state or multi-tenant deployment this title would need to change without a code change.
fix: Replace text="BMS Administration" with text="{i18n>shell.admin.title}" — the key already exists in bms-admin i18n.properties.

issue: Four monetary/cost fields (estimatedRepairCost in schema.cds, replacementCostEstimate and annualMaintenanceCostEstimate in extensions.cds, estimatedCostAUD/actualCostAUD in maintenance.cds) are plain Decimal types with no @Measures.ISOCurrency annotation and no companion currency_code field. In OData/Fiori Elements, amounts without currency association render as plain numbers with no currency symbol, and Analytical List Page / Smart Charts cannot aggregate them correctly. All cost fields in a production asset management system must carry currency metadata.
fix: Add a companion 'currency_code : Currency' field (using CDS built-in Currency type) to each entity with monetary fields, or annotate with @Measures.ISOCurrency : {$Path: 'currency_code'} and add currency_code to the entity. If AUD is always the currency, add a virtual currency_code defaulting to 'AUD' and annotate accordingly.

issue: The bridge card HTML generation uses new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-AU', ...) — a hardcoded Australian English locale. When this application is deployed in a multi-state or future multi-jurisdiction context, the date format will still be en-AU regardless of user locale or server region.
fix: Use new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) for the date in the card HTML (ISO 8601 is locale-neutral). For display dates in the UI, rely on Fiori/UI5 DateFormat with locale from the user session.

issue: The estimatedRepairCost column description is hardcoded to 'AUD' and inspection standard description references 'AS5100-7 | AGAM | TfNSW-BIM' — NSW-specific Australian standards hardcoded in the server-side column definition. These hardcoded strings appear as Excel column tooltip descriptions and cannot be localised without a code change.
fix: Move locale-specific column descriptions to a configuration object that can be overridden per deployment. At minimum, document that these strings are AU-specific constants.

issue: Multiple views use hardcoded hex colors on Icon controls: AttributeConfig.view.xml color="#0a6ed1" (line 152), ChangeDocuments.view.xml color="#0064d9" (line 141) and color="#8696a9" (line 203), dashboard/Main.view.xml color="#BB0000" and color="#E76500". Hardcoded hex colors are not theme-aware: in high-contrast accessibility themes (sap_horizon_hcb, sap_belize_hcb) these colors will remain unchanged and will likely fail WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large/icon elements).
fix: Replace all hardcoded hex color values with SAP semantic color tokens. Use valueColor="Good"/"Error" on NumericContent, type="Positive"/"Negative" on ObjectStatus, or use SAP design token CSS custom properties. Never hardcode hex colors on Icon controls.

issue: The user search Input uses only a placeholder attribute ('Search user...') with no associated sap.m.Label element, no ariaLabelledBy, and no ariaDescribedBy binding. Screen readers will read placeholder text when the field is empty but not announce the field purpose when focus enters a populated field. Fails WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). The same pattern occurs in DataQuality.view.xml (filterState, filterName inputs with placeholders but no Labels).
fix: Add a Label element with for= pointing to the Input's id, or set ariaLabelledBy on the Input referencing a nearby invisible Label using sap.ui.core.InvisibleText. Apply this pattern to all search/filter Inputs that use placeholder-only labelling.

issue: Three Input controls inside the WMS layer table rows (lines 179-181) and dialog inputs (lines 202-245) have only placeholder text with no associated Labels. These inputs are embedded in table cells with no visible or programmatic label relationship. Screen readers cannot identify these fields by purpose.
fix: Add explicit ariaLabelledBy references or wrap with sap.m.Label using the labelFor property. For table-cell inputs, use ariaLabel='Display name' (etc.) directly on the Input to provide an accessible name.

issue: No ARIA live region or sap.ui.core.InvisibleMessage announcements are made when async data loads complete in any bms-admin controller except for mass-upload. Controllers ChangeDocuments.controller.js, DataQuality.controller.js, and AttributeReport.controller.js call setBusy(true)/setBusy(false) but do not announce load completion to screen readers. Users with screen readers have no way to know when a search or data export has finished.
fix: Import sap.ui.core.InvisibleMessage and call invisibleMessage.announce('Search results loaded: N records', InvisibleMessageMode.Polite) after each async data load completes. The mass-upload controller Main.controller.js line 791 already demonstrates this pattern.

issue: Dialogs opened in AttributeConfig, LookupValues, and DataQuality controllers handle afterClose by calling destroy(), but do not restore keyboard focus to the triggering element when the dialog closes. When a user opens a dialog via keyboard and closes it, focus falls to the body/document root instead of returning to the button that opened the dialog. Fails WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
fix: Before opening each dialog, store a reference to the triggering element. In the afterClose handler, call storedElement.focus() to restore focus.

issue: The admin-bridges Fiori Elements app does not use Flexible Column Layout (FCL) for master-detail navigation between the Bridge ListReport and ObjectPage. The app uses NavContainer-based routing which navigates away from the list on selection. FCL would allow side-by-side list+detail view on desktop — a core Fiori design pattern for asset management apps.
fix: Evaluate migrating admin-bridges to use sap.f.FlexibleColumnLayout with routerClass 'sap.f.routing.Router'. This is an L effort. Flag as a UX debt item if FCL migration is not planned before go-live.

issue: The 'Active This Week' GenericTile uses valueColor="Critical" (orange) as a visual-only state indicator. The meaning of the activity level is conveyed solely by colour difference between adjacent tiles (green=Good vs orange=Critical) with no additional text label or icon differentiation. Users with colour vision deficiency cannot distinguish the states without colour.
fix: Add a subheader or indicator label that describes the state in text: e.g. subheader="Activity: High". Use distinct icons per activity state to supplement colour coding.

issue: The admin-bridges i18n error messages for lat/lon validation use global range values: error.latitude.range states 'Latitude must be between -90 and 90' (the global range, not Australia's -44 to -10). The CLAUDE.md learnings specify that Australian coordinates must use GDA2020 bounding box. The i18n error message contradicts the intended server-side validation bounds.
fix: Update error.latitude.range to 'Latitude must be between -44 (south) and -10 (north) — Australian GDA2020 bounds'. Update error.longitude.range to 'Longitude must be between 112 (west) and 154 (east) — Australian GDA2020 bounds'.

issue: ISO 25010 Quality Assessment — scores below threshold: Usability 2/5 FLAGGED (hardcoded text throughout, no ARIA labels on search inputs, no screen-reader live announcements in 7+ controllers, colour-only state indicators). Portability 2/5 FLAGGED (hardcoded en-AU locale, AUD currency strings, NSW references in handler code, no UI5 framework version pinning in ui5.yaml, operations apps pinned to minUI5Version 1.120.0 vs main apps 1.136.0). Functional Suitability 4/5. Performance Efficiency 3/5. Compatibility 3/5. Reliability 3/5. Security 4/5. Maintainability 3/5.
fix: Address Usability (score 2): See STD-008, STD-009, STD-013, STD-014, STD-016. Address Portability (score 2): See STD-011, STD-012, STD-023, STD-025. Target score >=3 on all dimensions before PAC certification submission.

issue: BridgeManagement-logging uses service-plan 'lite' for the application-logs service. The 'lite' plan retains logs for only 7 days. Under the Privacy Act 1988 APP11 (security of personal information) and NSW government audit requirements, system access logs should be retained for a minimum of 12 months. The UserActivity table in the DB provides application-level tracking but infrastructure logs are discarded after 7 days.
fix: Upgrade BridgeManagement-logging to service-plan: 'standard' before go-live. The standard plan offers configurable retention (up to 90 days), or route to SAP Cloud Logging service for longer retention.

issue: Operations apps (bridges and restrictions) declare minUI5Version: '1.120.0' while all other BMS apps use '1.136.0'. This version fragmentation means operations apps may not support UI5 controls or accessibility fixes available in 1.136.0+. The operations apps were likely cloned from an older template and the minVersion was not updated.
fix: Update minUI5Version in app/operations/bridges/webapp/manifest.json and app/operations/restrictions/webapp/manifest.json from '1.120.0' to '1.136.0' to match the rest of the BMS application portfolio.

issue: The xsappname in xs-security.json is 'bridge-management' (lowercase, static) but mta.yaml overrides it to 'BridgeManagement-${org}-${space}' (dynamic). If xs-security.json is used directly in local XSUAA testing or a manual service update, the static name 'bridge-management' will be used, producing a different XSAPPNAME in scope resolution and potentially breaking requireScope() middleware validation.
fix: Add a comment documenting that the mta.yaml config block overrides this xsappname value at deploy time. Consider using '${xs-app-name}' placeholder in xs-security.json, or align both to the same naming convention.

issue: The Fiori launchpad sandbox pins UI5 to version 1.145.0 via CDN URL. In production BTP, the html5-apps-repo runtime serves apps using its own bundled UI5 version — the fiori-apps.html pin has no effect in BTP. No ui5.yaml framework version section exists in any app to enforce a specific version during the BTP build, creating a local-vs-BTP version discrepancy risk.
fix: Add a framework section to each app's ui5.yaml: 'framework: { name: SAPUI5, version: 1.145.0 }'. This ensures the ui5-task-zipper packs the correct UI5 version into the zip artifact deployed to html5-apps-repo, making local and BTP UI5 versions consistent.

issue: BridgeInspectionElements, BridgeCarriageways, BridgeContacts, and BridgeMehComponents have no @restrict annotation. They are exposed in AdminService with no row-level access control. Any authenticated user with the 'view' scope can read and potentially mutate all inspection elements across all bridges, regardless of state assignment or role. This violates the principle of least privilege.
fix: Add @restrict annotations following the pattern used on BridgeInspections and BridgeDefects: grant READ to view,inspect,manage,admin; grant CREATE,UPDATE to inspect,manage,admin; grant DELETE to manage,admin.

issue: The results Table (s1Table) has no aria-label or ariaLabelledBy identifying it in the page structure, and the transition from busy (loading) to zero-result empty state produces no screen reader announcement. When search completes with no results, screen reader users receive no feedback that the search has finished or that zero results were found.
fix: Add ariaLabel='Change Document Records' to the Table element. After search completes, use InvisibleMessage.announce('No records found matching your filters', Polite) or 'N records found' to provide completion feedback.
